summary: Misaligned batcher window triggers eviction wave and sustained p99 jitter for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
A dedicated-tenant (NimbusAI) is experiencing repeated p99 latency spikes and throughput flicker across their reserved pool beginning 2026-03-10 08:40 UTC. Symptoms correlate with autoscaler scale-down windows and an eviction wave that affects both short-lived inference streams (interactive chat) and long-lived batched streams (bulk embedding).

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency p99 increased from ~450ms to 2.1s intermittently during peak window (08:30–09:30 UTC).
- Sustained reduction in overall throughput (~18% drop) for the tenant over a 45m window.
- No explicit OOMs or kernel panics observed; GPUs briefly detach from serving pool and are reattached after eviction waves.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: nimbus-dedicated-cluster-07 (G5/mixtures), autoscaler policy: predictive with conservative cooldown (300s).
- Region: us-west-2.
- Routes impacted: /v1/chat/stream (short streams), /v1/embeddings/batch (long batch jobs).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) High mix of short low-token streams and a few long embedding batches scheduled concurrently.
2) Autoscaler decides to scale down a stripe based on overall CPU signals at t0.
3) Batchers on affected GPUs flush and trigger synchronous eviction of in-memory KV caches to other GPUs while short streams remain active.
4) Eviction causes transient GPU attach/detach events and kernel queue stalls, leading to p99 latency spikes and an apparent throughput flicker.

Observed behavior:
- Repeated sequence of "eviction -> kernel-queue-wait -> GPU-detach -> reattach" logged across 3 GPUs in the stripe.
- Short streams get serialized onto fewer slots causing slot-hoarding for ~10–30s windows.
- Batcher latency backpressure causes upstream queueing and occasional 502s for retrying clients.

Expected behavior:
- Scale-down should drain gracefully without evicting active KV caches that are serving live requests; short streams should not be serialized onto fewer GPUs beyond configured p99 SLOs.

Relevant logs / metrics (attached snippets):
- serving-runtime logs: "evicting-kv-cache: tenant=nimbus, reason=scale-down, target_node=gpux-12" (2026-03-10T08:41:12Z)
- scheduler: "gpu-detach: node=gpux-12, cause=preempt, live_streams=6" (2026-03-10T08:41:13Z)
- autoscaler events: "scale_down_initiated -> completed (cooldown 300s)" (2026-03-10T08:40:50Z -> 08:41:50Z)
- Console traces: p99 latency spike to 2.1s at 08:41:15Z correlating with eviction events.

Notes:
- Customer reports this pattern intermittently over last 72 hours but frequency increased on 2026-03-10 after a config change to predictive autoscaler thresholds (lowered margin for idleness).
- Customer workload mix is atypical: ~70% short chat streams (2–10 tokens) and 30% long embedding batches (20k tokens), causing interleaved scheduling pressure.
comments: Support (Tanya): Customer raised ticket after noticing repeated p99 spikes during their morning window. Collected initial logs and escalated to SRE.
SRE (Evan): Reproduced correlation between autoscaler scale-down and eviction logs. Noted GPUs gpux-12/13/14 showing repeated detach cycles. Beginning deeper kernel and NVLink diagnostics.

Customer (NimbusAI - Alex Chen): We saw a similar blip last week but it resolved. After your last change to predictive policy, frequency increased. Happy to provide sample traffic replay and allow limited maintenance window.

SRE (Evan): Requesting permission for a 30m maintenance window to disable predictive scale-down and force a graceful drain to validate mitigation. Also requesting access to representative traffic replay (sanitized).

Eng (Priya Kumar): Flagging potential bug in batcher drain logic where eviction is synchronous instead of async during scale-down. Opening a tracking PR to add non-blocking drain and KV cache handoff metrics. See related PR linked.
Support (Tanya): Provided customer the tentative maintenance window 2026-03-11 09:00–09:30 UTC and instructions for safe replay files.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Predictive autoscaler prematurely triggers scale-down during short-term idleness causing synchronous KV eviction across multiple GPUs leading to transient detach.
Hypothesis 2: Batcher drain path has a blocking eviction step which serializes short streams while long batch handoff completes, amplifying slot contention.
Data points: console traces show strong time alignment between scale-down completion and first eviction log + p99 spike (+-3s).
Dashboard links: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenant/nimbus/throughput-latency and Slack thread #support for live correlation: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123SUPPORT/p1678464000000
Repro plan: 1) Disable predictive scale-down for nimbus pool, 2) Run traffic replay with 70/30 short/long mix, 3) Capture kernel and NVLink metrics, 4) Test non-blocking drain patch in canary.
resolution: Mitigation (temporary): Disabled predictive scale-down for nimbus-dedicated-cluster-07 at 2026-03-10T10:05Z. Passed a rolling canary that forces graceful drain during planned maintenance; p99 returned to baseline in canary window.
Customer action: NimbusAI scheduled traffic reshuffle to reduce long-batch overlap during peak window as additional buffer (recommended).

Planned fix: Engineering to land non-blocking batcher drain and async KV handoff patch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4621). Add a new metric for "eviction-block-duration" and a shield in autoscaler to avoid simultaneous stripe-scale-downs across GPUs hosting active live streams.
Follow-up work: Add an autoscaler runbook step to check live_streams > 0 before initiating scale-down; add automated test with mixed short/long stream workload in nightly regression harness.

Status: Partial mitigation applied; engineering PR in review and scheduled for canary deployment 2026-03-14. Will keep ticket open until post-canary verification completed and new metric has 48h of stable data.
